(consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-an-escrow-or-impound-account-en-140/, last reviewed Sep 11, 2024). Wording used: an escrow account 'is set up by your mortgage lender to pay certain property-related expenses'; lenders require 'that you pay your taxes and insurance using escrow'; 'The money that goes into the account comes from a portion of your monthly mortgage payment'; 'Your mortgage servicer will manage the escrow account and pay these bills on your behalf'; 'Your property taxes and insurance premiums can change from year to year' and the escrow payment and total monthly payment 'will change accordingly.' No dollar figures. Bank: the 2 Oct taxdate card covered the tax due date, a different angle.
headline:
What An Escrow Account
Actually Pays For
turn_1: Echo, the CFPB says an escrow account is set up by your mortgage lender to pay certain property costs, like your taxes and insurance.
turn_2: So where does that money come from? Do I mail it in separately?
turn_3: A portion of your monthly mortgage payment goes into it, and your servicer pays the bills. Taxes and insurance can change each year, so your payment can too.
echo_line: So part of the payment is the loan and part is the bills. If my payment ever changed, I'd look at the escrow first.
source: CFPB, What is an escrow or impound account?, consumerfinance.gov · retrieved Oct 17, 2026
disclaimer: General information, not financial or lending advice. Ask your lender or servicer how your own escrow account works.
